reviews.reason: Product-to-sum gives pi, pi/2 and zero in the three orthogonality cases; distinct polynomial degrees give a basis. Uniform approximation bounds the squared norm by pi*M*epsilon, and continuity gives a strictly positive integral near any nonzero value, including endpoints. The repaired F11 explicitly supplies the cosine preimage for this last step. Checked the local argument directly; no independent acceptance of my repair is claimed.

Distinct Legendre degrees give unique coefficients; positive weights give the square-root isometry onto real ell^2 and dense truncations. Norm and projection formulas are preserved. The only changed Definition clause concerns monotonicity. The direct projection-rate consumer already compares only (1+n(n+1))^s and retains 2/(2n+1) on both sides, so its proof remains sound unchanged.

The explicit local series converges by the existing geometric-null lemma. Checked the finite complex geometric sum, Poisson-kernel algebra and uniform-integral error yielding a_0=1/sqrt(3) and a_n=2(2-sqrt(3))^n/sqrt(3). Reflection kills odd cusp coefficients; product-to-sum integration gives 4(-1)^(m-1)/(pi(4m^2-1)), with the zero mode 2/pi. The Example section is unchanged.

Cosine monotonicity makes the reversed nodes strictly increasing for every N>=1, including N=1, so the real cardinal-interpolation theorem applies. Examined all seven direct item consumers, the unlinked spectral-regularity interpolation use, and page prose. All use real data/functions or only unchanged nodes. Three full-Definition quote mirrors were reconciled in the owning contract; consumer item files are unchanged.

The moment-data interface includes a finite positive relative Borel measure on a compact interval, at least m+1=N+2 support points and moments through 2m-1=2N+1. The finite supplier gives monic orthogonality through degree N. Each product degree i+j<=2N is within Gaussian exactness; orthogonality gives zero off diagonal and the defined h_i on diagonal. N=0 reduces to p_0=1. The Statement is unchanged.
